earlier_scan.source_named: Li, Fang-Kuei 1930. Mattole: An Athabaskan Language. University of Chicago Press. Full phonology+morphology; no readable scan reachable (HathiTrust/archive blocked).

sources.citation: American Anthropologist n.s. 32-34 (1930-1932), Digital Library of India scanned on archive.org (;ernet.dli.2015.533414/533415/533416).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No occurrence of 'Mattole' in any of the three volumes' scanned; no review of Li 1930 located there.
No phonology, stress, accent or tone content; references only classification/extinction.

sources.citation: Krauss, Michael E. 2017 (draft, held by the project). Eyak/Athabaskan comparative notes [file in ].
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Second-hand and about tone only: 'In summer 1928, while Sapir was working on Hupa in California ("no tones!" confesses Sapir), Li worked nearby on Wailaki and Mattole (no tones either). Li's Ph.D. dissertation (1930b) was the Mattole.' Also cites 'Li's Mattole grammar (1930.54)' for a verbal prefix. Nothing on stress placement.

sources.citation: Cook, Eung-Do & Keren Rice (eds.). 1989. Athapaskan Linguistics: Current Perspectives on a Language Family. Berlin: Mouton de Gruyter (Story's chapter on the first duoplural, pp. 491-493, cites Li 1930).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Mattole cited only for morphology (classifier and first-duoplural forms from Li 1930); no stress/accent statement for Mattole.

sources.citation: International Journal of American Linguistics 6(1), 1931 (archive.org scanned, sim_international-journal-of-american-linguistics_1931_6_1); also IJAL 6(2), 6(3-4), 7(1-2), 7(3-4) a full-text search for stress/accent.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: One passing mention (optative formed by suffixing a glottal stop in Hupa, Mattole, Wailaki); no review of Li 1930 and nothing on Mattole stress in IJAL 6-7.

sources.note: Comparative-historical account of which Athabaskan languages lack tone (Pacific Coast Athabaskan incl. Mattole, per the Krauss 2017 draft held by the project); would give an authoritative 'tonal or not' line and possibly a stress note for Mattole.

sources.citation: Rice, Keren & Sharon Hargus. 2005. Introduction. In Hargus & Rice (eds.), Athabaskan Prosody (Current Issues in Linguistic Theory 269). Amsterdam: Benjamins.

sources.note: Family-wide survey of stress and tone systems in Athabaskan; the most likely modern secondary source to summarize Li's Mattole accent data alongside other Pacific Coast Athabaskan languages.
